results.question: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?

[PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "Participants were extensively phenotyped with questionnaires, physical exam, stress test, echocardiogram, cardiac MRI, coronary calcium score, and blood measurement of markers of inflammation and fibrosis." [PMID:41791688]. [PMID:41791688]. [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "Limited data from this pilot study suggest that HIV may be associated with increased cardiac fibrosis and decreased right ventricular function." [PMID:41791688].

results.question: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: The study reports: "AV access flow was quantified as brachial artery flow volume (FV) using pulsed Doppler ultrasonography." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "The mean FV was 0.71 ± 0.29 L/min, and the median dialysis vintage was 5.0 years (interquartile range, 3.0-11.0 years)." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Higher FV was significantly associated with increased LVMI (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27)." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "A total of 241 patients were included." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Multivariate regression models were applied to investigate the associations of FV and dialysis vintage with LVMI, and to assess potential interactions between these variables."
